Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we start the final MAP for the October rollout, the execs asked for a clear performance gate so we can sign off. Key asks from FinEdge:
- Steady-state: sustain ~120 concurrent user sessions (avg gen length ~256 tokens) with minimal tail latency.
- Burst headroom: tolerate short bursts to ~400 concurrent sessions for up to 30s without widespread failures.
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): 95th percentile should be under ~600ms.
- End-to-end for 256-token responses: 95th percentile < 3.5s.
- Visible queueing/429s during peak bursts is acceptable only at very low rates (<2–3%).

We need those numbers baked into the MAP and an explicit set of tuning recommendations (rate limits, retry behavior, queue depth) so our SREs can validate on-prem traffic shaping. Can you share Redwood's evaluation plan, the concurrency test results you collect, and a proposed close timeline?

Appreciate it — Alice

Folks —

Attached is the concrete test plan and initial run results from our staging cluster. Short summary:
- Test harness: Locust + custom token-level meter; synthetic prompt mix pulled from FinEdge sample corpus (see config).
- Steady-state scenario (120 concurrency, seq=256): ran 45m, results: TTFT median 280ms, p95 560ms, p99 1.2s; end-to-end median 1.2s, p95 2.8s. Error rate: 0.4% (mostly transient 5xx).
- Burst scenario (400 concurrency peak for 30s): observed queueing and ~7% 429 responses during the peak window; p95 TTFT jumped to ~2.1s with some requests delayed >4s.
- Observed behavior: when the orchestrator queue length capped, worker-side backpressure caused head-of-line blocking and 429s clustered by client.

Prelim recommendations (high level):
1) Soft rate-limit per-client: steady window at 120 concurrent-equivalent with short burst allowance (3x steady capacity) and token-aware accounting.
2) Queue depth: increase request queue to 512 for this customer on Dedicated pool, with FIFO per-client sub-queues to avoid single-client head-of-line blocking.
3) Backoff: implement exponential backoff for 429s with jitter and a 2–6s retry window.
4) Enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts to reduce per-request work.

I'll share raw CSVs and the test config in the next message. If engineering thinks the queue-depth/worker adjustments are feasible, we can include them in the MAP as required tuning before production.

Subject: Re: Performance gating for production rollout — engineering findings and tuning recos

Thanks Marissa — reviewed the CSV and logs. Deck of detailed observations below (engineer -> non-engineer friendly):

Environment: Dedicated 8xA10 pool, model=redwood-1.3-8bit, seq=256 steady, batcher configured for continuous batching with max batch size 32.

What we observed:
- Steady-state (120 concurrency):
  • Median TTFT: ~310ms (a bit higher than Marissa's run due to CPU scheduling on the prior run), p95 TTFT: ~580–620ms.
  • End-to-end median 1.25s, p95 ~2.9s.
  • No significant queueing; error rate <1% (transient infra 5xx).
- Burst (400 concurrency for 30s):
  • Queue growth at orchestrator layer (Kube ingress + internal request queue). When queue depth exceeds 256, worker-side backpressure results in head-of-line blocking and 429s.
  • Observed 429 rate: 6–9% during peak; 95th TTFT across burst window rose to ~2.0–2.4s.
  • Once queue tail trimmed, throughput recovered within ~90s.

Root causes and implications:
1) Single shared queue leads to a few large requests (longer generations) delaying many short requests — classic HOL blocking.
2) Batcher sizing: at high burst concurrency, batching latency grows non-linearly; we saw increased batching window of up to +40ms which amplifies TTFT for small responses.
3) Rate-limit coupling: current per-token quotas are coarse; we need client-aware token accounting to avoid starvation during bursts.

Engineering recommendations (actionable):
- Short term (MAP):
  1) Per-client FIFO sub-queues + queue-depth cap 512 for FinEdge; this prevents HOL blocking from other tenants on the same pool.
  2) Soft token-based rate-limit: steady allowance equivalent to 120 concurrent sessions, burst token pool = 3x steady, enforce at gateway with token buckets and server-initiated 429 with Retry-After header.
  3) Tune batcher max latency to 40ms at high load (currently 80ms) to limit batching-induced TTFT increases.
  4) Document required client-side retry policy: exponential backoff (base=0.5s, max=6s) with jitter; recommend idempotent retry keys for safety.
- Medium term (post-cutover):
  • Implement adaptive batch sizing (workload-aware) and per-client batch isolation where heavy clients are isolated to a separate pool.
  • Add a token-aware admission controller that prioritizes first-token latency (TTFT) for interactive workloads.

MAP implications / timeline:
- Tests finalized and MAP draft: 10/08 (done).
- Internal engineering signoff on queue/rate-limit changes: target 10/12.
- Customer validation window (FinEdge runs using our staging endpoint + their SRE sim): 10/13–10/16.
- Production enablement / reservation and SLA signoff: target 10/23.

I've attached a short PDF with the recommended rate-limit parameters and a sample gateway config for their SREs. If we agree, we should capture the short-term items as required pre-cutover steps in the MAP.

Thanks again for the clear gating criteria. Attached is the consolidated MAP entry and a one‑page summary of the performance evaluation we ran in staging. High level:
- Steady-state (120 concurrent, seq=256): TTFT p95 observed ~580–620ms; end-to-end p95 ~2.8–3.0s. Error rate <1%. Meets the TTFT target in most runs but close to the 600ms threshold; we recommend including the queue-depth and batcher tuning below as part of the MAP to provide margin.
- Burst to 400 concurrency (30s): we observed 6–9% 429s and elevated TTFT; with the short-term engineering changes below we estimate burst 429s can be reduced to <=3% and p95 TTFT reduced by ~25%.

Required pre-cutover items (to include in MAP):
1) Apply per-client FIFO sub-queue and increase queue depth to 512 for FinEdge on Dedicated pool.
2) Configure soft token-bucket limits: steady allowance = 120 concurrent-equivalent, burst pool = 3x steady.
3) Tune batcher max latency to 40ms under high load.
4) Customer to adopt retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter (0.5s base, max 6s), and surface Retry-After headers.

Proposed close timeline:
- 10/12: Redwood engineering signoff on applied queue + batcher changes.
- 10/13–10/16: FinEdge validation window (customer side tests against staging endpoint).
- 10/20: Final MAP signoff meeting (executive + SRE).
- 10/23: Production enablement / cutover (subject to successful validation).
